messages:
Alex R: ok team — Q1 roadmap sync: we need to pick the minimal shipped surface for kernel selection + quant + KV cache. customer asks (FinFlow, HealthSync) are pushing for predictable p95 and lower token cost.
Priya S: agree. main constraint: kernels take dev time but give big latency wins on long seqs. quant yields cost wins but risks regressions on some tasks. KV cache is the fastest user-visible improvement for chat workloads.
Matt L: can we break into 3 milestones? 1) lightweight KV cache + eviction policy, 2) quant profiles for production-safe models, 3) dynamic kernel selector service. each milestone has clear launch criteria.
Kai W: +1. propose launch criteria: KV: p95 seq=256 < 80ms on our ci rig, cache hit >= 40% for chat workload; Quant: regression < 1% on eval set + cost reduction >= 18%; Kernel selector: stable rollout with canary rollback within 5m.
Hannah J: customers care about tail latency spikes more than average. Maybe add SLA target: <5% requests > 2x median. Also add observability: token-level tracing and per-model perf dashboard before GA.
Alex R: good call. tradeoffs: if we prioritize KV first we get immediate wins for chat customers. If we do quant first we reduce infra cost but need more eval infra. Which gives best early ROI?
Priya S: performance estimate: KV alone reduces cost ~12% due to fewer forward tokens for typical sessions. Quant (8-bit/4-bit) can cut compute cost 25-40% depending on model but onboarding per-model is heavy. Kernel work can reduce p95 by 20-35% for Llama-family on A100 -> highest latency impact.
Matt L: so sequence: KV fast ship, then kernel perf on top of that, then quant as a follow-up to reduce unit cost. This minimizes customer impact and gives iterative wins.
Kai W: implementation notes: KV cache needs prefix sharding, fast lookup hot path, and eviction TTL heuristics. Rough sketch:
```
cache.put(session_id, prefix_kv, seq_end)
if (cache.hit) use_kv()
else compute_and_maybe_store()
```
We should avoid blocking critical RPCs on cache writes (async writes).
Hannah J: rollout plan: feature-flagged release to hosted first, dedicated later. For Private we ship as opt-in with clear migration doc. Add a fallback to uncached path if memory pressure high.
Perf-bot: daily perf run scheduled: kernel-a100-rtperf / kv-experiment / quant-smoke will run at 03:00 UTC. Results posted to #perf-results.
Alex R: scope negotiation — Eng infra: how many engineers and sprints for KV MVP?
Matt L: estimate: 3 engineers x 3 sprints for KV MVP + tooling (tracing, dashboards). Kernel selector: 4 engineers x 4-5 sprints. Quant profiles: 2 engineers x 4 sprints + eval infra. These are overlappable but we need prioritization.
Priya S: product perspective: customers asking for predictability and cost. Recommend KV + observability as Q1 focus, kernel work starts mid-Q1, quant planning + eval infra in Q1 with execution Q2.
Kai W: risks: cache correctness (consistency across replicas), memory bloat on dedicated pools, quant-induced hallucination increases. Mitigations: strong CI, per-model quality gates, memory quotas.
Hannah J: acceptance tests to add: synthetic long-chat with intermittent interruptions, regressions for common LLM prompts (summarize, code, math). Also include canary traffic split and automated rollback.
Alex R: decision: go for KV MVP first (feature flag) + perf observability baseline. Start kernel perf spike in week 3. Open action items: 1) Matt draft KV design doc by EOD Friday, 2) Kai spike for async writes + TTL perf tests, 3) Priya collect customer SLAs and share top 5 eval prompts.
Priya S: will pull FinFlow/HealthSync SLAs and add to doc.
Matt L: I'll start the doc. cc @perf-bot to collect baseline numbers once KV benchmark is ready.
Perf-bot: acknowledged. baseline run queued.
Alex R: thanks all — we'll review designs Mon 09:30. :thumbsup:
